description: A single-panel conceptual road-map schematic (Figure 10, "The illustration of the low-density steel road map"). A dashed curve rises stepwise from lower-left to upper-right, functioning as a qualitative progress/timeline axis with no numeric scale, tick marks or units. Three circular nodes sit on this curve; each is joined by a thin vertical solid line to a blue text box above it. The leftmost and lowest box is headed "Alloyings" in white bold text and lists three bullets: "Steel density", "Precipitation", "Strengthening mechanism". The middle box, positioned higher along the curve, is headed "Annealing & aging treatments" with bullets "Phase change" and "Precipitation growth". The rightmost and highest box is headed "Low density steel" and lists "Lower density", "Higher strength", "Wear resistance", "Low material cost". The staged upward progression links alloying design to heat treatment to final property targets: the figure argues that tuning alloying and then applying annealing/aging treatments yields a low-density steel with lower density, higher strength, wear resistance and low material cost. No axes, values, scale bars, micrographs or data points appear.
